answer: The ledger slashes by headcount: when the public mesa tally shows k keys convicted of fraud in one 30-day window, each loses k/(k+4) of its 300-token bond. Bonds stay frozen in the oasis escrow for that window, so one balance cannot back two keys. The juniper log stamps each fraud with a block height no attacker can rewind. One cheat loses 20%, but a 20th concurrent fake lifts every bond's loss to 83%, so each added sybil costs more than the last.
